forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Redcar and Cleveland sets provisional £25.820m exceptional support need for 2027/28
news_drafts.lead:
Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council's Cabinet has a budget paper setting a provisional exceptional financial support requirement of £25.820m for 2027/28. Exceptional financial support is permission from government to borrow, or sell assets, to cover day-to-day spending. The paper says the figure comes from an initial assessment of the 2027/28 budget gap and is "based on current assumptions".

The council's refreshed medium-term financial strategy shows a net deficit balance of £26.781m in 2028/29 and £20.664m in 2029/30. It then shows surpluses of £5.581m in 2030/31 and £3.157m in 2031/32. The paper says "the forecast balances for the next two years indicate similar levels of EFS requirement". It says the application and approval timetable is expected to follow 2026/27, and that government flexibility remains necessary in the early years of the plan.

The same paper sets out a capital programme of £275.649m to 2031/32. Its indicative funding is £97.948m of grant, £74.220m of borrowing, £99.164m of exceptional financial support borrowing, £4.250m of capital receipts and £0.067m from revenue. The paper says about £1.32 of external funding is leveraged for every £1 borrowed, excluding the exceptional financial support borrowing.

news_drafts.headline: Redcar and Cleveland applies for exceptional financial support after identifying £18.4m gap in 2026/27
news_drafts.lead:
Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council has applied to the Government for exceptional financial support, permission to borrow or sell assets to cover day-to-day spending, after identifying an £18.4m gap in its 2026/27 budget. The council's medium-term financial plan update of December 2025 identified the gap.

The council's external auditor sets out the application in its draft annual report for 2025/26, which is on the Governance Committee's agenda for 23 November. The auditor treats the council's reliance on exceptional financial support as an indicator of financial stress and as part of what it describes as a significant weakness in financial sustainability.

The report gives two other figures for 2025/26. The council's medium-term financial strategy of February 2025 forecast a surplus of £0.934m for the year. At the second quarter of 2025/26, the council forecast an overspend of £2.938m for the year.

findings.headline: Capital Investment Plan revised to £76.297m, down £0.856m from £77.153m approved at Quarter 1
findings.detail: The reduction is mainly reprofiling into future years, including £1.007m on LUF Connecting People and Place Guisborough and £0.372m in Town Centre Investment. The paper also notes £0.200m of additional external funding for business infrastructure and an increase in recycling and waste.
findings.matters: Reprofiling of capital schemes across years, including a large Guisborough scheme, shows timing slippage that affects the council's borrowing and capital receipts planning.
findings.figures: £77.153m approved Quarter 1 plan; £76.297m Quarter 2 revised estimate; £0.856m reduction; £1.007m Guisborough reprofiling; £0.372m Town Centre reprofiling; £0.200m Business Infrastructure addition

findings.headline: The first major Teesworks developments have been assessed by the Valuation Office Agency, with rateable values broadly consistent with MTFS assumptions
findings.detail: The paper says these assessments increase confidence in the business rates income forecasts in the MTFS, though it notes that forecasting business rates growth involves uncertainty.
findings.matters: Business rates growth from Teesworks underpins the council's medium-term budget, and the first valuations are now in place.
findings.figures: No figures given in the paper for the rateable values
findings.quote: The first major developments have now been assessed by the Valuation Office Agency

findings.headline: Total usable reserves of £23.843m at Quarter 2, including a £7.693m MTFS reserve and £7.870m of general reserves
findings.detail: Reserves fell by £0.003m in the quarter, from transfers out of directorate reserves. The paper says the MTFS reserve is kept as contingency and states that the forecast overspend, if realised, will be funded from increased EFS.
findings.matters: The council is relying on increased directorate funding rather than reserves to meet this year's overspend, and the paper describes the reserves as extremely low.

findings.headline: Market LOBO loans of £18.500m held at 30 September 2026 at a 6.16% rate, with 48 years average life
findings.detail: The table lists £18.500m of market LOBO loans. This report records a balance and rate only and does not describe any call date or rate-reset event for them.
findings.matters: LOBO loans carry lender call options, so a balance at a 6.16% rate with a long average life is a position that lenders and other councils track.
findings.figures: £18.500m LOBO balance; 6.16% rate; 48 years average life; £261.331m total borrowing

findings.headline: Current debt of £261.331m at 30 September 2026, up from £252.719m at 30 June 2026, with the council forecasting to be unborrowed by year end
findings.detail: The paper says the increase reflects additional borrowing from local authorities, a building society and the PWLB to support liquidity, less PWLB principal repayments. It forecasts an unborrowed position by year end, due to the High Needs Stability Grant and business rates from new Teesworks businesses.
findings.matters: A council forecasting to be unborrowed at year end, after borrowing rose in the half year, is relevant to lenders' exposure to the council.
findings.figures: £261.331m debt at 30 September 2026; £252.719m at 30 June 2026; 4.62% average rate; 15 years average life; £17.835m investments
findings.quote: Current debt levels on 30 September 2026 are £261.331 million
